issues.legal_issue: A Wakf Tribunal may determine whether disputed premises are Wakf property when that status dispute turns on whether the premises fall within the extent of property identified in the notified Wakf record.
material_facts: The claim sought eviction from premises said to be Wakf property and recovery of an additional portion alleged to have been encroached upon.
The respondent denied that either portion was Wakf property and disputed the notification identifying the extent of the Wakf property.
The Tribunal framed and decided whether the premises formed part of the notified Wakf property, relying on the evidence presented.
issues.conclusion: The suit was maintainable before the Wakf Tribunal, which had jurisdiction to determine whether the disputed premises formed part of the Wakf property.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 6 and 7 of the Wakf Act, 1995 assign to the Tribunal disputes about whether property specified as Wakf property is Wakf property; Section 85 bars civil-court jurisdiction over matters required to be determined under the Act. Ramesh Gobindram v. Sugra Humayun Mirza Wakf (2010) 8 SCC 726 concerned eviction from property admitted to be Wakf property and did not govern this dispute about the notified property’s extent. Board of Wakf, West Bengal v. Anis Fatma Begum (2010) 14 SCC 588, Haryana Wakf Board v. Mahesh Kumar (2014) 16 SCC 45, and Punjab Wakf Board v. Sham Singh Harike (2019) 4 SCC 698 support determining whether the Act requires the dispute to be decided by the Tribunal. Faseela M. v. Munnerul Islam Madrasa Committee (2014) 16 SCC 38 was distinguished, and Kiran Devi v. Bihar State Sunni Wakf Board (2021) SCC Online SC 280 confirms that jurisdiction depends on the facts and the statutory framework.

predicates.waqf_tribunal_possession_suit: A party brought a suit before a Wakf Tribunal seeking possession of premises claimed to belong to a Wakf institution.
predicates.defendant_disputes_waqf_status: The opposing party denied that the premises were Wakf property.
predicates.dispute_concerns_notified_property_exten: The dispute concerned whether the premises fell within the extent of property identified in the notified Wakf record.

issues.definition: When a possession suit before a Wakf Tribunal involves a denial of Wakf status based on the notified property’s extent, the Tribunal may determine that status.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court exercising revisional jurisdiction over a Wakf Tribunal’s decision may not reappreciate evidence as an appellate court and may interfere with the Tribunal’s findings only within the limited scope of that jurisdiction.
material_facts: The respondent challenged the Tribunal’s decree through a revision petition.
The High Court reassessed the evidence concerning the extent and identity of the Wakf property and set aside the Tribunal’s decision.
The Tribunal had considered the evidence, including records relating to the amended extent, an earlier dispute involving the respondent’s father, a plan, and photographs.
The Supreme Court found that the Tribunal’s factual findings were supported by the record and that the High Court had not identified a basis for the limited revisional interference.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in reappreciating the evidence or setting aside the Tribunal’s decision; its order was set aside and the Tribunal’s judgment was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 227 of the Constitution and the proviso to Section 83(9) of the Wakf Act, 1995, the High Court examines the correctness, legality, or propriety of the Tribunal’s findings and does not act as an appellate court. Interference is limited to an appropriate revisional basis, such as a facially perverse finding or a conclusion unacceptable to any reasonable person. Kiran Devi v. Bihar State Sunni Wakf Board (2021) SCC Online SC 280 states that the High Court exercises this limited jurisdiction when reviewing a Wakf Tribunal order.

rule.if: revision_from_waqf_tribunal and high_court_reappraises_evidence and tribunal_finding_supported_by_record and no_facial_perversity

predicates.revision_from_waqf_tribunal: A party sought revisional review of a Wakf Tribunal’s decision.
predicates.high_court_reappraises_evidence: The High Court reassessed the evidence rather than confining its review to the limited revisional function.
predicates.tribunal_finding_supported_by_record: The Tribunal’s finding was based on evidence available in the record.
predicates.no_facial_perversity: The Tribunal’s finding was not facially perverse and was not a conclusion that no reasonable person could accept.

issues.definition: When a supported Tribunal finding is reviewed in revision and is not facially perverse, a High Court’s reappraisal of the evidence does not justify interference.
